The top part of the crop also takes in printed page text that is not part of the figure: the end of the problem 2 reference data, the full Задача 3 statement and the 'Решение:' heading, plus a sliver of the solution text to the right and below. pdfRect [67.32,134.64,309.06,601.92] is too narrow and starts too high. The truncated labels are still partly guessable, but the figure loses printed label text and duplicates page text. Major is the right severity.

printed: The Ksp for calcium oxalate is 2.3×10-9 and the Ksp for magnesium oxalate is 8.6×10-5.
published: The solubility products ... are ... respectively. Calcium can therefore be precipitated selectively as calcium oxalate.

Nothing on the page prints 'Calcium can therefore be precipitated selectively as calcium oxalate.' The values are correct, so the problem is the added sentence and the paraphrased bullets.

printed: EDTA binds to Mg2+ and Ca2+ even in the presence of Calmagite. The stoichiometry of the EDTA-metal complex formed with both Mg2+ and Ca2+ is 1:1.
published: EDTA binds magnesium and calcium, including magnesium bound to Calmagite, in 1:1 mole ratios.

It also prints 'Calcium ions are not bound by Calmagite.' The published text rewrites these as 'including magnesium bound to Calmagite, in 1:1 mole ratios' and 'Calcium does not bind to this indicator'. That is a reinterpretation, not a transcription.

printed: A. Precipitation of calcium ions — Precipitate the calcium ions in a 25.00 cm3 aliquot of the "Bottled Water" sample by accurately adding ... (from the common burettes in each lab room). Carefully swirl ... Allow at least 45 minutes for complete precipitation to occur.

Precipitation of calcium ions', then 'Precipitate the calcium ions in a 25.00 cm3 aliquot of the "Bottled Water" sample by accurately adding approximately 0.50 cm3 ... (from the common burettes in each lab room). Carefully swirl the solution to ensure uniform mixing. Allow at least 45 minutes for complete precipitation to occur.' The published section is titled 'Precipitation of calcium oxalate' and the paragraph is fully rewritten ('Pipette 25.00 cm³ of bottled water into a flask...'). The 'Procedure' heading is missing.

printed: Using distilled water, dilute 5.00 cm3 ... to a final volume of 100.0 cm3. Add 40 cm3 of distilled water, 5 cm3 of pH 10 buffer solution, and some Calmagite indicator to 5.00 cm3 of diluted magnesium solution.

Add 40 cm3 of distilled water, 5 cm3 of pH 10 buffer solution, and some Calmagite indicator to 5.00 cm3 of diluted magnesium solution.' The page has no volumetric flask and no 'approximately'; the published text adds both. The heading 'Standardization of the EDTA solution' is also shortened.

printed: C. Titration of Mg2+ and Ca2+ — Add 40 cm3 of distilled water ... to 5.00 cm3 of the "Bottled Water" sample.
published: C. Determination of total magnesium and calcium — Pipette 5.00 cm³ of bottled water into a flask. Add approximately 40 cm³ of water

printed: D. Titration of Mg2+ — ... The presence of a small amount of calcium oxalate will not interfere with your titration.
published: D. Determination of magnesium — ... A small amount of calcium oxalate precipitate does not interfere.

The published text renames the heading to 'Determination of magnesium', adds 'approximately 40 cm³' and paraphrases the sentence. Raised to major for consistency with index 3.

printed: aqueous ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid; 500 cm3 sample of "Bottled Water"
published: Aqueous EDTA solution.; A 500 cm³ bottle of water.

printed: When glycyrrhizin was methylated with methyl iodide (MeI) at every possible site before hydrolysis, hydrolysis produced A' (methyl glycyrrhizinate), C and D (Scheme 2).
published: Methylation with MeI and Ag2O, followed by acid hydrolysis, produces A′ (C31H48O4), C (C9H16O7), and D (C10H18O7) (Scheme 2).
evidence: Book p. 1023 (PDF page 617, rendered as tmp/tx/icho-2008-theory/pages/problems-617.png because prepare.mjs refuses this paperId) has this sentence at the bottom: 'When glycyrrhizin was methylated with methyl iodide (MeI) at every possible site before hydrolysis, hydrolysis produced A' (methyl glycyrrhizinate), C and D (Scheme 2).' The published statement replaces it with 'Methylation with MeI and Ag2O, followed by acid hydrolysis, produces A′ (C31H48O4), C (C9H16O7), and D (C10H18O7) (Scheme 2).' The reagents and formulas in the published version do match Scheme 2 on p. 1024 (PDF page 618), so nothing chemical was invented. But the printed prose was rewritten rather than transcribed. It drops the exhaustive-methylation condition 'at every possible site', which is what tells the student that every free OH and COOH group was methylated before hydrolysis, so the deduction of C, D and J depends on it. Scheme 2 shows only 'MeI, Ag2O', which does not state this condition. It also drops the identification 'A' (methyl glycyrrhizinate)'. A missing condition that the structure deduction depends on keeps this at critical.
